skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover, run, and track hosted AI apps for images, video, LLMs, search, 3D, audio, and social workflows.
skill.summary: Guide agents through inference.sh CLI app discovery, execution, authentication, file uploads, and result tracking.
skill.author: inference-skills

security_audit.summary: Several markdown links and secret references are benign documentation, but the skill contains real high-risk installation and execution patterns. Confirmed issues include pipe-to-shell installers, remote manifest command substitution, PATH installation of a downloaded binary, broad belt CLI execution, automatic local file uploads, and authenticated social media actions. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl piped to sh with versioned package-manager or manual install steps that verify checksums and signatures before execution.
Avoid shell substitution from remote manifest data. Publish fixed release artifact URLs and separate verification commands.

remediation.issue: Downloaded binary placed in user PATH
remediation.suggestion: Document the install location, permissions, update process, and removal steps. Prefer an isolated tool directory or package manager.
Require explicit user confirmation for each local path and identify the destination app before upload.
Require explicit confirmation before posting, following, liking, retweeting, or sending direct messages through Twitter/X apps.

semantic_findings.title: Broad CLI Tool Authorization
semantic_findings.description: The skill front matter grants Bash access to any belt command. This broad wildcard can run discovery, app execution, deployment, login, updates, uploads, and account-changing workflows through one CLI namespace.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration is explicit and covers Bash(belt *). The risk depends on user approval and CLI behavior, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Local File Uploads to Cloud Apps
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that the CLI automatically uploads local files when paths are provided and gives image, audio, and media examples. This can disclose local files to hosted apps if paths are accepted without explicit user review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited sections directly describe automatic upload of local file paths. This is an intended feature, but it is a clear data exposure risk.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Social Media Actions

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly list post-tweet and broader Twitter/X automation. The exact account impact depends on credentials and selected app permissions.

content.user_title: Run Inference.sh AI Apps from Agents
content.value_statement: Agents often need a consistent way to find and run hosted AI apps. This skill teaches the inference.sh CLI workflow for discovery, inputs, execution, and task results.
actual_capabilities: Explains inference.sh CLI installation, login, and API key authentication workflows.
Lists, searches, filters, and inspects hosted AI apps by category or query.
Runs hosted apps with inline input or saved input files through belt app run.
Shows local media path uploads for image, video, audio, and social workflows.
Tracks long-running tasks and retrieves results with belt task get.
Points to related skills for images, video, LLMs, search, avatars, and Twitter/X automation.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account.
Cloud app runs may consume account credits or quota.
Local file paths can be uploaded to hosted apps when used as inputs.
Does not audit third-party app behavior beyond the published CLI schema.

use_cases.title: Prototype multimodal AI workflows
use_cases.description: Find image, video, audio, search, and LLM apps, then run quick tests from one CLI workflow.

use_cases.title: Automate agent media tasks
use_cases.description: Use hosted generation and processing apps for images, videos, captions, avatars, and local media inputs.

use_cases.title: Inspect app schemas before execution
use_cases.description: List available apps, review required inputs, generate samples, and track task results before production use.

prompt_templates.title: Find an app
prompt_templates.prompt: Find inference.sh apps for image generation. Show the most relevant options and explain which one fits a fast prototype.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a run
prompt_templates.prompt: Get the required inputs for the selected inference.sh app and prepare a concise run plan. Ask before using any local file path.

prompt_templates.title: Run and track a task
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the chosen inference.sh app with my approved inputs, then track the task until the result is available.

prompt_templates.title: Build a workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-step inference.sh workflow that uses search, an LLM, and media generation. Include approval points for uploads and external account actions.

output_examples.input: Ask for a fast image generation option for a product mockup.
output_examples.output: The skill can return a short list of matching apps, a recommended choice, required input fields, and a confirmation step before running.

output_examples.input: Ask to run a video generation task from an approved prompt.
output_examples.output: The skill can submit the app run, report the task identifier, check progress, and summarize where the completed result can be retrieved.

output_examples.input: Ask to use a local media file with an avatar app.
output_examples.output: The skill can identify which local paths will be uploaded, request confirmation, then run the app only after approval.

best_practices: Review each local file path before allowing the CLI to upload it.
Use sample inputs and app schema details before running expensive tasks.
Confirm social media, deployment, and account-changing actions before execution.
anti_patterns: Piping remote installers to a shell without independent verification.
Putting API keys or account secrets directly into shared prompts or logs.
Running posting, upload, or deployment commands without explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help an agent do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent use the inference.sh CLI to discover apps, prepare inputs, run tasks, and retrieve results.

faq.question: Does it require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI must be installed and authenticated before most app runs will work.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI can upload local paths when an app input accepts files, so review every path first.

faq.question: Can it post to Twitter or X?
faq.answer: The skill documents Twitter/X automation apps. Any account action should require clear user confirmation.

faq.question: Does it choose the best AI model automatically?
faq.answer: It can help search and compare available apps, but the final choice depends on your requirements and account access.

faq.question: Is it safe to install automatically?
faq.answer: Automatic installation needs caution because the documentation includes remote installer and shell execution patterns.
